source.title: Efficacy of Contextually Tailored Suggestions for Physical Activity: A Micro-randomized Optimization Trial of HeartSteps

study.population: Healthy sedentary adults in Ann Arbor; available decision points within participants

claim: The secondary walking-suggestion comparison favored suggestions; the primary pooled-suggestion interval included the no-effect value.

outcome.name: Log-transformed 30-minute steps; exponentiated treatment coefficient
outcome.window: 30 minutes after each available randomized decision during a planned six-week study

findings.name: Walking suggestion versus no suggestion
findings.locator: Results: Effects of Walking Versus Antisedentary Suggestions

limitations: 44 recruited, 37 analyzed; repeated decisions are not independent participants.
Walking-only result is a secondary analysis.
Zero-imputed missing step data and effect attenuation require sensitivity checks.
Neither total daily activity nor long-term health or suffering reduction was established.
This is an external study, not Manager field impact.
